newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Taiwan futures set record volume.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Taiwan futures set record volume.

text.p: SIMEX MSCI Taiwan stock index futures ended firmer in active Thursday trade, which saw market turnover exceed 1,000 lots for the first time since the contract's launch on January 9.
Dealers said there was good institutional interest and the March contract recovered from a weak opening to close 3.2 points above its previous settlement of 320.2 on volume of 1,026 lots.
"We've had an unbelievable day, partly due to a somewhat large sell-off earlier this week," said a trader with a European house.
He said people set up short positions around 321.0 earlier in the week on the assumption the market would weaken further and then had to cover their positions when it failed to do so.
"It was very optimistic and it was not like we had a major announcement today," he added.
Perry Gilbert, vice president of Refco Futures, said the futures followed the cash market higher on the back of a recovery in electronic stocks.
"Investors began to lessen their concern regarding a tightening in the Taiwan central bank's monetary policy, despite overnight rates still at record levels," Gilbert said.
He said the March contract opened lower with locals expecting the easier cash market to produce institutional selling in the futures.
The Taipei stock market index ended 101.58 points higher at 7,832.07 on strong bargain-hunting, triggered by bullish signs of a gathering economic recovery.
